text: Ons Jabeur won the women's singles title at the 2022 Madrid Open by defeating Jessica Pegula 7–5, 0–6, 6–2, marking her first WTA 1000 title and making her the first Arab and African woman to achieve this feat. Aryna Sabalenka, the defending champion, lost in the first round to Amanda Anisimova. Pegula reached the final after being a match point down against Camila Giorgi in the first round. This was the last professional appearance of 2016 Olympic gold medalist Monica Puig, who lost to Danielle Collins in the first round. The seeded players were determined based on the entry list as of 25 April 2022, with rankings and points prior to that date also reflecting that date. Players who did not qualify in 2021 had their points reduced by the points from their 16th best tournament. Some players who would have been seeded withdrew before the tournament began, and one such player is exempt from receiving zero points due to a long-term injury.
